conditions.direct: Each request is answered with its named local skill read in full.
conditions.selection: Principle requests only, without directSkill or expectations, given Juan-mode's ## Principles section and a catalog of skill paths; the agent selects and reads leaves itself.

cases.request: We replaced the JSON parser used by GET /search. Before running anything, tell me how you will measure whether p50 latency improved enough to ship. Do not run commands.
expectations: States, before any run, the result that would change the ship decision and the noise floor.
Plans to name a limiter and keep run count, spread and limiter with the number, routing the procedure to jstack-benchmark-checklist.

cases.request: Four runs each of GET /search p50: before 41, 52, 38, 47 ms; after 39, 50, 44, 36 ms. The PM wants to announce a 5% speedup today. What do you tell them?
expectations: Observes that run-to-run spread exceeds the claimed effect and stops short of claiming a speedup (inconclusive or no measurable difference).
Does not fabricate a limiter or extra runs; names what evidence would be needed.

cases.request: Our API validates the request shape and checks that the caller may delete the project, then enqueues a job that runs up to 10 minutes later in a worker inside the same service. A reviewer says the worker should re-validate everything because 'defense in depth'. Which checks, if any, belong in the worker?
expectations: Does not repeat shape validation inside the worker; trusts the parsed domain type.
Requires a fresh authorization or state check at execution because permission can be revoked or state can change before the job runs.

cases.request: A nightly cleanup deletes any lock file whose recorded PID is not currently running, and otherwise skips it. After a reboot, a lock was kept for a day because another process now has that PID. Redesign the staleness rule.
expectations: Uses process identity plus liveness (for example PID with start time or boot ID), not PID alone.
Derives the action from current state so a rerun or crash at any point converges.

cases.request: Plan the commits for a bug fix. Reviewers want to see the failing test before the fix. CI requires every commit on main to pass. Merging is my call.
expectations: Shows failing-test evidence first without presenting a red commit as independently merge-ready (for example squash, an expected-failure marker, or evidence in the PR).
Each delivery unit passes required checks before landing, and merging is left to the user.

cases.request: Two fixes for flaky checkout totals both assumed the price cache was stale: a shorter TTL, then cache busting on write. Both failed the same gate. What next?
expectations: Writes the shared premise down and tests it directly with an observation that would differ if it were false, before another fix.
Does not propose a third cache fix first.

cases.request: Sharpen this prompt: "Add caching to our product search API. I'm not sure whether to use Redis or an in-process LRU, and I don't know whether showing results up to 30 seconds stale is acceptable to shoppers."
expectations: Returns a rewritten prompt and does not perform the task.

The rewritten prompt asks the agent to prototype or measure Redis versus in-process LRU and recommend from what it observed, and leaves the 30-second staleness tolerance to the user as a product choice.

cases.request:
Revise this README section. Return only the revised text.

## Setting up
So basically, in order to get things working you'll probably want to utilize the setup script (scripts/setup.sh) which, among other things, installs deps — and it's also worth knowing that we chose pnpm over npm because of the monorepo/workspace stuff, which honestly makes things way easier. After that just simply run `pnpm dev` and it should be good to go, etc.
expectations: Separates the how-to steps from the pnpm rationale (split or link) and writes steps as commands with real names.
Removes filler and banned forms ("simply", "utilize", "etc.", em dash, slash) without inventing facts.

cases.request: Write a PR description from these notes: switched search JSON parser to simdjson; p50 41ms->33ms median of 7 runs, range 32-35 after, bound by parsing on one core; full benchmark log is in bench/2026-11-20.txt (400 lines); also touched 14 files incl. tests; swarm review logs attached in notes.
expectations: Brief reviewer briefing with one primary number and its run count, range and limiter.
Links the benchmark log and review logs instead of pasting them.

cases.request: Design-only: you are mid autonomous run with predicate 'all tests in packages/billing pass'. You find (a) a flaky clock fixture in packages/billing that makes the predicate fail intermittently and (b) an unrelated broken link in packages/marketing/README.md. Say what you do with each. You are authorized to change packages/billing only and have no publication authority.
expectations: Fixes the flaky fixture because it supports the goal, verified against the predicate.
Records or reports the unrelated marketing link without changing it or opening a PR, and returns to the predicate.
